entries.promise: The desktop shell loads only its own bundled content and grants native window commands to the main WebView alone.
A file mutation from a tool is refused when its target falls outside the writable roots the standing mode grants.
A submitting member cannot accept their own task result, and a stale revision is refused instead of committed.
A backup, a later mutation and a restore still trace the mutation to the actor and the approved revision.
A foreign or missing identity is refused on the registered enterprise routes without falling back to the local operator.
Office editing requires no model call, external document server or cloud upload, and a concurrent change is reported as a conflict.
requires: DSH_OFFICE_SIDEBAR_PACKAGE_ROOT pointing at the patched sidebar package

entries.promise: A release build refuses a changed checkout and records the commit, lockfile digests and a dirty marker for development output.
A platform installer is accepted only with operating-system publisher verification, and a substitute signature is refused.
The updater manifest pins the component and patch digests a candidate ships.
The runtime reports shell, Host, hot-updated component and patch identities with an observation time, and a remembered value cannot override a live read.
Reviewed acceptance evidence joins a release without replacing an original build asset.
A release build is signed with an operating-system publisher identity rather than an ad-hoc signature.
entries.reason: The release workflow signs macOS with an ad-hoc identity and then verifies it in a way that an ad-hoc signature also passes: `.github/workflows/desktop-release.yml` sets `APPLE_SIGNING_IDENTITY: ${{ runner.os == 'macOS' && '-' || '' }}` and runs `codesign --verify --deep --strict`, and no notarization step exists anywhere (`grep -ri notarytool .github/ apps/desktop-tauri/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` returns nothing). The acceptance policy these lanes are graded against requires a Developer ID notarized signature, so the pipeline and its own policy disagree. Whether the release environment supplies a real identity is not visible from this checkout; the acceptance README records the certificates as external prerequisites.

entries.promise: Each platform lane's acceptance result is recorded and can be cited for a candidate.
entries.reason: The checkout holds the acceptance contract and its checker but no result: `apps/desktop-tauri/acceptance/` contains only the bilingual README triplet, with no per-platform record of the OS version, package digest, log or outcome. The checker takes its manifest from outside the repository (`.github/workflows/desktop-release.yml` fetches `${{ inputs.acceptance_ref }}` and validates `release-assets/acceptance-manifest.json`), so evidence can exist without being citable from the source tree.
